x: Coleman was forty yards ahead of Churcher at the two miles point, with like distances separating Gregory and McMullen, and then a little further back Barrett (Cambridge), Tunbridge and Brazier (Highgate) leading a biggish group.

At about half distance apart from Barrett of Cambridge Harriers, the front part of the race looked almost like a Belgrave Club race with Gerry Gregory, Harry Churcher, Dave McMullen and Syd James all on each other's heels.
Gerry Gregory took an early lead on the uphill climb over the first mile and gradually increased it on the outward journey being followed by Barrett and Harry Churcher.

At the halfway stage, Barrett, winner of the two previous opens, was lying third and was never able to make up any leeway. Once again we had our first scoring three in the first five and with Charlie Churcher back in the "A" Team, 10th making our fourth man, we thus regained possession of the Berman…

Foord of Brighton and Barrett, SAC. were first and second almost from the start and never looked as though they would be replaced. When the field had settled down, Jim Masters was running 3rd with Baker of the local club who eventually beat him and our scoring six were in the first thirty.
Heywood scored a runaway victory from Barrett of Ealing with Eldon taking third place inside Stan Cox's record of 54.19. Dave Baulch finished 4th, 9 secs outside the previous record.
Baulch especially was in fine fettle to finish 11th behind such names as Firth, Caulder, Barrett, Towl, Maynard, Clark and Driver, all of whom are in international class in one sphere or another.
